bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: Fox acquires Roku for $22B; 7 analysts downgrade ROKU to neutral/hold
bullets.body: Fox agreed to acquire Roku for $160/share (60% cash at $96, 40% FOXA stock at 0.9693x ratio), valuing the deal at ~$22B with $400M cost synergies and pro forma net leverage 2.8x at close expected 1H27. Wolfe, JPM, Piper Sandler, Susquehanna, Evercore, Citizens, and Loop all downgraded ROKU to neutral/hold/peer perform citing low probability of competing bid; deal implied value ~$149 after FOXA fell 17%. MS sees FCF accretion by FY29 ($9-10/sh), with linear revenue exposure dropping from ~65% to ~50% by 2030; FOXA now trades at ~10x CY27 EBITDA vs historical 6.5-8.5x.

bullets.title: STX/WDC: Morgan Stanley raises PTs aggressively; HDD cycle elongation through CY28
bullets.body: MS lifted STX PT to $1,035 and WDC PT to $650 based on Asia checks confirming HDD demand growing 40-50% annually vs supply growth of 30-35%, with shortages expected through at least CY28. Current nearline HDD price/TB under $15; Taiwan vendors targeting $25-30/TB over 2-3 years. STX and WDC FY28 EPS estimates now ~70% above Street consensus; STX remains MS 'Top Pick' for greater near-term margin expansion. Pre-market: WDC +8.5%, STX +6.3-7%.

bullets.title: MU/Memory complex: +10.8% yesterday; HBM4E pull-forward and MLCC shortages signal extended AI cycle
bullets.body: Micron surged 10.8% Monday alongside WDC +16%, STX +9.43%, SNDK +6.45% on risk-on macro and analyst upgrades. SK Hynix pulling forward HBM4E samples to June/July (vs prior 2H26 guidance) targeting NVDA Rubin Ultra with 384GB HBM capacity; Samsung completed first HBM4E sample shipment in late May at 4TB/s bandwidth. MLCC lead times extending to 24 weeks with 20-40% price increases; NVDA Rubin uses 12,000 MLCCs per board vs 6,500 on GB200. Pre-market MU +2.9%.

bullets.title: AMD: +6.9% Monday; signs definitive 30 MW AI compute deal with Rackspace through 2028
bullets.body: AMD and Rackspace signed a definitive agreement for phased deployment of 30 MW AMD-based compute (MI355X, MI350P, EPYC CPUs) across global data centers from late 2026 through 2028, operationalizing a May MOU and targeting regulated enterprise workloads. UBS also notes AMD CPU lead times extended to 20+ weeks and AI racks scaling toward 100k+ units by C27. AMD introducing memory-tiering technology to alleviate data-center memory constraints.

bullets.title: NVDA: Plans $20-25B investment-grade bond raise; rack shipments 75k C26, 100-110k C27
bullets.body: NVIDIA is planning to raise at least $20-25B through investment-grade corporate bonds—described as creating a liquid benchmark rather than a funding need given $49B quarterly FCF and $216B FY2026 revenue. Rack shipment forecasts are 75k in C26 rising to 100-110k in C27. UBS flags margin pressure and memory price pushback from hyperscalers; JPM maintains OW. NVDA was down -0.6% pre-market despite the broader tech rally.

bullets.title: CRM: Acquires Fin for $3.6B; UBS stays Neutral, Mizuho reiterates Outperform
bullets.body: Salesforce is acquiring AI customer-service platform Fin (formerly Intercom) for ~$3.6B cash (~9x EV/ARR), closing F4Q27 with no guidance change. Fin's proprietary Apex model outperforms GPT-5.4 on resolution rate (76% vs 71%) with 65% fewer hallucinations and has 30,000+ customers at $100M+ ARR growing 350% Y/Y. UBS (Neutral, $185 PT) questions why Fin was needed after two years of Agentforce R&D; Mizuho reiterates Outperform citing SMB land-and-expand wedge. CRM trading at 11x CY26 FCF.

bullets.title: PLTR: Wolfe relaunches at Peer Perform; channel checks show no LLM displacement risk
bullets.body: Wolfe Research relaunched PLTR coverage at Peer Perform, citing 150% NRR, 85% revenue growth, and 97% backlog growth but arguing the 30x CY27 revenue / 65x EPS valuation (2x software peers) limits upside. Fair value range $100-190. UBS channel checks separately show no evidence of LLM displacement, reinforcing platform stickiness. Positive catalysts include large AIP renewals and US government program ramps (Maven, TITAN, Vantage).

bullets.title: ACN: Diverging views into Thursday earnings; MS downgrades to EW, UBS flags low bar
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley downgraded ACN to Equal Weight from Overweight, cutting PT to $177 from $240, citing AI spend crowding out traditional IT services with CY26 IT budget growth only ~2% YoY. UBS takes the opposite view—stock at ~11x forward despite steady growth and margin expansion, with AI additive via integration demand; calls the bar low into Thursday's report (consensus EPS $3.71, revenue $18.78B). IT Services were the weakest tech sub-sector Monday: ACN/CTSH -2.89%, EPAM -2.7%.

bullets.title: AAPL: Citi Buy $315 PT; iPhone 17 outperforming down-14% smartphone market; WWDC AI strategy incrementally positive
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on AAPL at $315 PT (33x CY2027 P/E, 20% premium to historical) as iPhone 17 grows modestly YoY in April despite the global smartphone market declining 14% YoY in 2026. WWDC formalized AI strategy via Gemini integration, dedicated Siri app, and hybrid on-device/cloud architecture. Foldable iPhone expected fall 2026 at ~6M units but seen as niche. Key risk remains China unavailability of Apple Intelligence limiting upgrade cycle uplift.

bullets.title: ARM: Implied vol at 98th percentile after +19% w/w on analyst upgrades; data-center CPU thesis intact
bullets.body: ARM climbed 19% week-over-week with +11% moves on Jun 11-12 following analyst PT raises on data-center CPUs and AI infrastructure. Citi options data shows 1M implied vol at 100 (98th percentile), 25pts below realized vol of 124.8. Monday ARM rose 8.3% in the broader semis rally. Qualcomm's potential Tenstorrent acquisition ($8-10B) may add competitive framing for ARM's AI inference positioning.

bullets.title: AMZN: JPM OW; projects 47% US e-commerce share, $83B ad revenue in 2026; MSFT using AWS for GitHub AI capacity
bullets.body: JPM reiterates AMZN OW with N. America core retail margins expanding +80bps to 8.3% in 2026 and advertising revenue projected at $83B (+21% YoY) with ~46% operating margin (~36% of total OI). Separately, Microsoft has turned to AWS to handle GitHub's AI-driven capacity surge (commits on pace for 14B in 2026 vs 1B in 2025), despite plans to migrate fully to Azure by 2027—an embarrassment for Azure but a near-term AWS positive.

bullets.title: MSFT: Flagged with $90-130B FY27-28 funding gap; using AWS for GitHub AI capacity
bullets.body: JPM flags MSFT as '1 year behind' hyperscaler peers with a $90-130B FY27-28 capex funding gap vs GOOG/AMZN pre-funding $300-350B each. The GitHub-to-AWS capacity diversion (14B commits projected in 2026 vs 1B in 2025) underscores near-term Azure infrastructure strain. JPM maintains MSFT OW despite the concerns.

bullets.title: NBIS: Completes $643M acquisition of Eigen AI for inference optimization
bullets.body: Nebius completed its acquisition of Eigen AI (announced May 1) for approximately $643M in cash and shares. Eigen's inference and post-training optimization technology will integrate into Nebius's Token Factory platform, and Eigen's founding team will establish a Nebius engineering and research presence in the San Francisco Bay Area.

bullets.title: DELL: Wins $1.44B US Air Force firm-fixed-price contract
bullets.body: Dell was awarded approximately $1.44B in a US Air Force firm-fixed-price call order. The win adds to Dell's AI infrastructure positioning alongside broader data-center capex tailwinds.

bullets.title: TSLA: GS raises Q2 delivery estimate to 420K; maintains Neutral on mixed signals
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs raised its TSLA Q2 2026 delivery estimate to 420K from 405K, tracking ahead of ~400K consensus, on stronger regional data from Europe and China. GS maintains Neutral citing mixed US demand signals, FSD/robotaxi execution risks, and valuation. Tesla China FSD launch expected within 2-3 weeks. Pre-market TSLA -1.1%.

bullets.title: SHOP: Oppenheimer Outperform $175 PT; AI-first model driving 30%+ growth with flat headcount
bullets.body: Oppenheimer reiterates Shopify Outperform at $175 PT after management indicated no macro-related deterioration in consumer trends, broad-based Q1 growth, and headcount held flat through AI productivity gains enabling high-20s to 30%+ revenue growth. An increased share repurchase authorization adds downside support. Multiple sources flag Shopify as a key AI-native beneficiary within e-commerce infrastructure.

bullets.title: HOOD: Announces 10% workforce reduction; launches agentic options trading, secures IPO underwriting approval
bullets.body: Robinhood announced approximately 10% workforce reduction (~$20M severance, $8M share-based comp charges). Simultaneously, HOOD launched agentic trading for options (full Greeks and order management) and received FINRA approval to serve as an IPO underwriter, expanding into capital markets. Pre-market HOOD +1.4%.

bullets.title: OKLO: Signs MOU with Standard Nuclear for nuclear fuel recycling and advanced fuel manufacturing
bullets.body: Oklo announced a memorandum of understanding with Standard Nuclear covering nuclear fuel recycling and advanced fuel manufacturing collaboration, extending its fuel supply chain positioning.

bullets.title: INTC/MRVL: MS notes CEO confidence on foundry and scale-up; pre-market INTC -1.6%, MRVL -1.6%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Joe Moore flagged positive CEO meetings with Intel (committed to foundry, positive on microprocessors) and Marvell (showing 'new levels of confidence' particularly on scale-up) as incremental positives. Despite this, both names are trading lower pre-market (-1.6% each), potentially on profit-taking after the Monday semis rally or CPO push-out to 2030-31 headwinds for optical networking.

bullets.title: DIS: InterDigital awarded EU patent injunction over HEVC video encoding
bullets.body: The Mannheim Local Division of the Unified Patent Court ruled InterDigital entitled to an injunction against Disney covering HEVC video encoding across 11 EU countries—the first UPC injunction against Disney. Disney can appeal; prior injunctions from German and Brazilian courts covered HDR technology and AVC compression.
